bounded_recoveries.procedure: run native commands separately, retain each exit code, and construct the bounded summary only afterward
hash the exact binary Git blob and keep normalized-LF and line-reconstructed domains explicit
inspect helper source before invocation and replay immutable manifests through one read-only Git cat-file batch
query path, local branch, and remote branch as separate bounded scalar reads
inspect persisted worktree state and use git read-tree -mu HEAD once rather than replaying creation
consume Git output inside one bounded Python subprocess and emit prefix counts only
preserve non-cone mode from repository configuration and add the literal build-script pattern with --skip-checks
retain both collisions at zero credit and replace them with distinct model-revision acknowledgement and queue-persistence hypotheses before refreezing
retain the failed assertions at zero credit and refresh only the exact count mirrors plus the current test class name

failures.failed_witness: the first combined source summary embedded a native ancestry command inside a PowerShell object expression and failed before any Git query ran
failures.recovery: run native commands separately, retain each exit code, and construct the bounded summary only afterward

failures.failed_witness: the first packet digest reconstructed text through PowerShell lines and produced a false byte-domain mismatch
failures.recovery: hash the exact binary Git blob and keep normalized-LF and line-reconstructed domains explicit

failures.failed_witness: the first manifest helper probe assumed every lifecycle helper supported --help and one builder refused at the wrong lifecycle head
failures.recovery: inspect helper source before invocation and replay immutable manifests through one read-only Git cat-file batch

failures.failed_witness: the first combined branch-availability wrapper returned no attributable output
failures.recovery: query path, local branch, and remote branch as separate bounded scalar reads

failures.failed_witness: the first sparse-checkout setup crossed its wrapper boundary after registering the branch and patterns but before materializing the index
failures.recovery: inspect persisted worktree state and use git read-tree -mu HEAD once rather than replaying creation

failures.failed_witness: a git ls-files projection exceeded the model output window even though only summary fields were intended
failures.recovery: consume Git output inside one bounded Python subprocess and emit prefix counts only

failures.failed_witness: git sparse-checkout add rejected a version-inapplicable --no-cone option
failures.recovery: preserve non-cone mode from repository configuration and add the literal build-script pattern with --skip-checks

failures.failed_witness: the first exact semantic audit found two Sable titles that exactly collided with the 9,110-row inherited chain and stopped before writing phase artifacts
failures.recovery: retain both collisions at zero credit and replace them with distinct model-revision acknowledgement and queue-persistence hypotheses before refreezing

failures.failed_witness: the first x1 test run retained two inherited-template count assertions for twenty-three startup incidents and thirteen sources while the current ledgers contained eight incidents and eleven current sources
failures.recovery: retain the failed assertions at zero credit and refresh only the exact count mirrors plus the current test class name

recovery_rule: Every recovery is additive and never erases or relabels the failed witness.
